summary: @ornikar/eslint-config-babel-use 13.2.1 ships preinstall Bun-runtime dropper executing obfuscated sibling payload
details: The package presents itself as an ESLint configuration under the @ornikar scope but declares a preinstall lifecycle hook (`node setup.mjs`) that, at npm install time, downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, marks it executable, and invokes it against a ~727KB obfuscated sibling file `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` carries a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header and consists of a heavily obfuscated string-array/rotator bundle with `_0xXXXX`-style identifiers, unreadable and unrelated to any ESLint configuration purpose. An ESLint config has no legitimate need to fetch an alternate language runtime and execute an opaque bundled payload against it on install. The package name and repository field reuse the legitimate ornikar/eslint-configs identity while adding lifecycle-driven runtime download and payload execution absent from prior releases, matching the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern under a compromised or impersonated trusted scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
